name: Cartomancer
body:
Cards are, for most, a diversion or source of easy money. Others use them for divinations. For the cartomancer, they are the stuff of magic. Their touch turns an ordinary deck of playing cards into a stack of spells they can literally and figuratively draw upon. Their magic waxes and wanes with the luck of the draw, should they use the hand they are dealt or risk it by drawing another?

Alignment: Cartomancers can be any alignment, but their reliance on the whims of luck lend to them being chaotically aligned.

Role: The cartomancer tends to be a support caster, the luck basis for what abilities and spells they can be difficult to plan for, but they do well when supported by allies with more dependable abilities. Their high charisma and skill set makes them a useful “face” of the party, even if the face they show is a false one or one prone to trickery.

The cartomancer eschews weapons and magic in favor of magics and their empowered cards. Their spell deck provides a set of power that relies on a varied skill set tempered by the luck of the draw. They are gamblers, either literally or in their sense of adventure and love of risk. You can’t win if you don’t play.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8.

Starting Wealth: 2d6 × 10 gp (average 70 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The cartomancer’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), and Spellcraft (Int).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are the class features of the cartomancer.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Cartomancers are proficient with simple weapons and light armor but no shields. Shields and armor do not impede a cartomancer’s spellcasting. A cartomancer is also always proficient with their spell deck if applicable.

Card Casting (Su)

You can use a deck of playing cards as a tool for weaving spells. They are considered a focus for a cartomancer’s spellcasting and are a stand-in for any material components. Your initial hand size is restricted to 5 cards. This increases by 1 at 7th, 15th, and 19th levels. See ‘card casting’ on page xx.

When determining the DCs and other spellcasting effects, a cartomancer uses their Charisma modifier.

Cartomancer Game

At 1st level, a cartomancer gains a set of skills called a cartomancer game. They provide abilities at 1st, 6th, 11th, and 18th level. These cartomancer games can be found on page xx.

Spell Deck

A cartomancer begins play with one spell deck. They gain the skill associated with the deck as a class skill and the spell deck determines what spell effects a cartomancer can produce. You can find the spell effects in the Card Casting section starting on page xx.

If a cartomancer loses their spell deck, they can bond to a new set of playing cards with a 10 minute ritual of shuffling and cutting the deck. You can only be bonded to one deck of cards at a time. This bonding does not change your spell deck type.

The DC for any saving throws is 10 + 1/2 the cartomancer’s class level + their Charisma modifier.

The following are the spell deck types available:

Arcane Deck

This deck is diverse and balanced. Arcane deck cartomancers can be found anywhere there is a game being played.

Associated Skill: Knowledge (arcana)

Divine Deck

This deck channels divine power for good or ill. Divine deck cartomancers often follow deities of luck.

Associated Skill: Knowledge (religion)

Occult Deck

This deck is the result of esoteric power pulled from sources beyond mortal ken. Occult deck cartomancers seek out more knowledge and means to expand their abilities.

Associated Skill: Knowledge (arcana)

Primal Deck

This deck is focused on the elements, wildlife, and plants. Primal deck cartomancers are prone to wandering, turning up in unexpected places, ready to play.

Associated Skill: Knowledge (nature)

Card Tricks (Su)

At 2nd level, as a standard action cartomancer can perform a series of card tricks and maneuvers that cause one or more creatures to be fascinated. Each creature to be fascinated must be within 90 feet, able to see and hear the cartomancer, and capable of paying attention to them. The cartomancer must also be able to see the creatures affected. The distraction of a nearby combat or other dangers prevents the ability from working. For every three levels a cartomancer has attained beyond 1st, they can target one additional creature with this ability. Each creature within range receives a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the cartomancer’s level + their Cha modifier) to negate the effect. If a creature’s saving throw succeeds, the cartomancer cannot attempt to fascinate that creature again for 24 hours. If its saving throw fails, the creature sits quietly and observes the card tricks for as long as the cartomancer continues to maintain it. While fascinated, a target takes a –4 penalty on skill checks made as reactions, such as Perception checks. Any potential threat to the target allows the target to make a new saving throw against the effect. Any obvious threat, such as someone drawing a weapon, casting a spell, or aiming a weapon at the target, automatically breaks the effect. At the end of each of its turns, a target can make a save to end this effect. Fascinate is an enchantment (compulsion), mind-affecting ability. This ability can be maintained as a standard action, otherwise there is no limit on the duration this ability may be maintained.

Energetic Empower (Su)

At 2nd level, when a cartomancer plays a spell card that deals damage and empowers it with a card with the acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, positive energy, negative energy, or sonic traits (see Card Casting starting on age xx), they can change the damage dealt by the played card to match the chosen trait from the empowering card. If you have the card sharp cartomancer game then this can also change the damage type dealt by the thrown card.

Ace Up My Sleeve (Ex)

Beginning with 3rd level, immediately before shuffling their deck, the cartomancer can set aside an ace from the deck, discard pile, or hand. The cartomancer then shuffles their deck and considers the set-aside ace as being in their hand without counting against their maximum hand size.

Read the Room (Ex)

At 4th level, a cartomancer learns techniques to read the tells of others. They gain a +2 bonus on Sense Motive checks. This bonus increases by +2 every 4 levels thereafter.

Aces Wild (Ex)

At 5th level, once per round a cartomancer can treat an ace as a wild card when casting a card spell.

Raise (Su)

At 9th level, a cartomancer can empower a card already in play with a card from their hand. The card in play must have an empower option and the empowering card must be a valid empowering card.

Trump Card (Su)

At 10th level, when a cartomancer fails a saving throw, they may discard an ace or king from their hand as an immediate action to reroll the saving throw.

Quick Fingers (Su)

At 13th level, all cards with a casting time of a standard action gain the following empowerment:

Empower (3 cards) The casting time of this card becomes a swift action.

Stud Hand (Ex)

Beginning with 14th level, if a cartomancer has no cards in their hand, they can choose to increase their hand size by 2 the next time they draw. If 4 they do, they cannot draw again until their hand is empty.

High Cards (Ex)

At 17th level, a cartomancer can take 1 minute to remove all cards of values 2 through 8 from one of their decks. These cards are not considered to be in their deck, hand, discard pile, nor in play. The cartomancer cannot gain benefit from these cards. They can take another minute to place those cards back in their deck.

Ace of Aces (Ex)

At 20th level, a cartomancer can place a discarded ace on the top of their spell deck rather than in the discard pile.
